The documented dnd5e block kit

Markup below follows the System HTML wiki page exactly. Note the fvtt prefix on advice/quest/narrative, and that notable goes on an <aside>, not a div.

Notable

A callout box for additional information. Everyone in Greenrest takes Selma's tonic every seventh day, from childhood.

Advice

Bordered card with a round icon hanging off the left edge. Image goes in the figure, text in the article.

Quest

Same format as Advice, styled as an objective. Four shards, four of these.

Narrative — a text box for read-aloud. The square opens ahead of you, and at its centre stands the gray tree, four guards at its roots who do not look at it.

There is no crying here.

Mayor Oswin Applewhite

Pull quotes use quote-lg plus float-right or float-left on an aside, with quote-author on the attribution line. Body text wraps around them, which is how the official books set epigraphs.

Secrets — core Foundry, not the system

Players never see this, even on a shared page, and the GM gets a Reveal button to show it mid-session. This is what every gmnote block should become.

Where these come from

Two ways in

The wiki says these styles "can be applied to any text field by using the menu options under the Custom menu or by editing the Source HTML </>." So there IS a toolbar path — open any page for editing and look for a Custom dropdown. The docs name it once and never show it, which is why nobody finds it.
